title: An inquiry into the existence of the gifted child

passage.title: An inquiry into the existence of the gifted child
paragraphs: Let us start by looking at a modern 'genius', Maryam Mirzakhani, who died at the early age of 40. She was the only woman to win the Fields Medal - the mathematical equivalent or a Nobel prize. It would be easy to assume that someone as special as Mirzakhani must have been one of those 'gifted' children, those who have an extraordinary ability in a specific sphere of activity or knowledge. But look closer and a different story emerges. Mirzakhani was born in Tehran, Iran. She went to a highly selective girls' school but math wasn't her interest - reading was. She loved novels and would read anything she could lay her hands on. As for math, she did rather poorly at it for the first couple of years in her middle school, but became interested when her elder brother told her about what he'd learned. He shared a famous math problem from a magazine that fascinated her - and she was hooked.

In adult life it is clear that she was curious, excited by what she did and also resolute in the face of setbacks. One of her comments sums it up.'Of course, the most rewarding part is the "Aha" moment, the excitement of discovery and enjoyment of understanding something new.... But most of the time, doing mathematics for me is like being on a long hike with no trail and no encl in sight. That trail took her to the heights of original research into mathematics.

Is her background unusual? Apparently not. Most! Nobel prize winners were unexceptional in childhood. Einstein was slow to talk as a baby. He foiled the general part of the entry test to Zurich Polytechnic - though they let him in because of high physics and math scores. He struggled at work initially, but he kept plugging away and eventually rewrote the laws of Newtonian mechanics with his theory of relativity.

There has been a considerable amount of research on high performance over the last century that suggests it goes way beyond tested intelligence. On top of that, research is clear that brains are flexible, new neural pathways can be created, and JQ isn't fixed. For example, just because you can read stories with hundreds of pages at the age of five doesn't mean you will still be ahead of your contemporaries in your teens.

While the jury is out on giftedness being innate and other factors potentially making the difference, what is certain is that the behaviours associated with high levels of performance are replicable and most can be taught - even traits such as curiosity.

According to my colleague Prof Deborah Eyre, with whom I've collaborated on the book Great Minds and How to Grow Them, the latest neuroscience and psychological research suggests most individuals can reach levels of performance associated in school with the gifted and talented. However, they must be taught the right attitudes and approaches to their learning and develop the attributes of high performers - curiosity, persistence and hard work, for example - an approach Eyre calls 'high performance learning'. Critically, they need the right support in developing those approaches at home as well as at school.

Prof Anders Ericsson, an eminent education psychologist at Florida State University, US, is the co-author of Peak: Secrets from the New Science of Expertise. After research going back to 1980 into diverse achievements, from music to memory to sport, he doesn't think unique and innate talents are at the heart of performance. Deliberate practice, that stretches you every step of the way, and around 10,000 hours of it, is what produces the goods. It's not a magic number - the highest performers move on to doing a whole lot more, of course. Ericsson's memory research is particularly interesting because random students, trained in memory techniques for the study, went on to outperform others thought to have innately superior memories - those who you might call gifted.

But it is perhaps the work of Benjamin Bloom, another distinguished American educationist working in the 1980s, that gives the most pause for thought. Bloom's team looked at a group of extraordinarily high achieving people in disciplines as varied as ballet, swimming, piano, tennis, math, sculpture and neurology. He found a pattern of parents encouraging and supporting their children, often in areas they enjoyed themselves. Bloom's outstanding people had worked very hard and consistently at something they had become hooked on when at a young age, and their parents all emerged as having strong work ethics themselves.

Eyre says we know how high performers learn. From that she has developed a high performing learning approach. She is working on this with a group of schools, both in Britain and abroad. Some spin-off research, which looked in detail at 24 of the 3,000 children being studied who were succeeding despite difficult circumstances, found something remarkable. Half were getting free school meals because of poverty, more than half were living with a single parent, and four in five were living in disadvantaged areas. Interviews uncovered strong evidence of an adult or adults in the child's life who valued and supported education, either in the immediate or extended family or in the child's wider community. Children talked about the need to work hard at school, to listen in class and keep trying.

Let us end with Einstein, the epitome of a genius. He clearly had curiosity, character and determination. He struggled against rejection in early life but was undeterred. Did he think he was a genius or even gifted? He once wrote: 'It's not that I'm so smart, it's just that I stay with problems longer. Most people say it is the intellect which makes a great scientist. They are wrong: it is character.

question_groups.body:
Maryam Mirzakhani
Maryam Mirzakhani is regarded as ____ (27) in the field of mathematics because she was the only female holder of the prestigious Fields Medal - a record that she retained at the time of her death. However, maths held little ____ (28) for her as a child and in fact her performance was below average until she was ____ (29) by a difficult puzzle that one of her siblings showed her.
Later, as a professional mathematician, she had an inquiring mind and proved herself to be ____ (30) when things did not go smoothly. She said she got the greatest ____ (31) from making ground-breaking discoveries and in fact she was responsible for some extremely ____ (32) mathematical studies.
question_groups.body_html:
Maryam Mirzakhani

Maryam Mirzakhani is regarded as [27] in the field of mathematics because she was the only female holder of the prestigious Fields Medal - a record that she retained at the time of her death. However, maths held little [28] for her as a child and in fact her performance was below average until she was [29] by a difficult puzzle that one of her siblings showed her.

Later, as a professional mathematician, she had an inquiring mind and proved herself to be [30] when things did not go smoothly. She said she got the greatest [31] from making ground-breaking discoveries and in fact she was responsible for some extremely [32] mathematical studies.

quotes: She was the only woman to win the Fields Medal - the mathematical equivalent or a Nobel prize.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi và giải thích ngữ pháp (nếu cần):
Tuy nhiên, môn toán lại không mấy ___________ đối với bà khi còn nhỏ.
Bước 2: Xác định từ loại dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: NOUN
Dấu hiệu: held + NOUN (NOUN là Object của Transitive Verb ‘HELD’)
Lưu ý: NOUN nên ở dạng Uncountable (vì theo sau ‘LITTLE’)
Bước 3: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
maths ~ từ khóa giữ nguyên
wasn't ~ held little
Bước 4: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "toán học không phải là sở thích của bà ấy - đọc sách mới là sở thích" (math wasn't her interest - reading was).
Bước 5: Đáp án: A. appeal
Tuy nhiên, môn toán lại không mấy hấp dẫn đối với bà khi còn nhỏ (However, maths held little appeal for her as a child)
quotes: She went to a highly selective girls' school but math wasn't her interest - reading was.

As for math, she did rather poorly at it for the first couple of years in her middle school, but became interested when her elder brother told her about what he'd learned. He shared a famous math problem from a magazine that fascinated her - and she was hooked.
In adult life it is clear that she was curious, excited by what she did and also resolute in the face of setbacks.
'Of course, the most rewarding part is the "Aha" moment, the excitement of discovery and enjoyment of understanding something new.

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi và giải thích ngữ pháp (nếu cần):
Và thực tế bà đã chịu trách nhiệm cho một số nghiên cứu toán học cực kỳ ___________.
Bước 2: Xác định từ loại dựa trên các dấu hiệu:
Loại từ: ADJECTIVE
Dấu hiệu: extremely + ADJECTIVE (ADJECTIVE được bổ nghĩa bởi Adverb ‘EXTREMELY’)
Bước 3: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
took her to ~ responsible for
heights of ~ extremely
original research into mathematics ~ mathematical studies
Bước 4: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Con đường đó đưa cô ấy đến đỉnh cao của những nghiên cứu độc đáo về toán học" (That trail took her to the heights of original research into mathematics).
Bước 5: Đáp án: I. innovative
Và thực tế bà đã chịu trách nhiệm cho một số nghiên cứu toán học cực kỳ tân tiến (and in fact she was responsible for some extremely innovative mathematical studies)
quotes: That trail took her to the heights of original research into mathematics.

questions.text: Many people who ended up winning prestigious intellectual prizes only reached an average standard when young.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Nhiều người đoạt được các giải thưởng danh giá về trí tuệ, hồi nhỏ chỉ có thành tích ở mức trung bình.
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
Nobel prize ~ prestigious intellectual prizes
unexceptional in childhood ~ average standard when young
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "hầu hết những người đoạt giải Nobel đều không có gì nổi bật khi còn nhỏ". Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "Nhiều người đoạt được các giải thưởng danh giá về trí tuệ, hồi nhỏ chỉ có thành tích ở mức trung bình (Many people who ended up winning prestigious intellectual prizes only reached an average standard when young)
Bước 4: Đáp án: YES
quotes: Nobel prize winners were unexceptional in childhood.

questions.text: Einstein's failures as a young man were due to his lack of confidence.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Những thất bại của Einstein khi còn trẻ là do ông thiếu sự tự tin.
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
Einstein ~ tên riêng giữ nguyên
slow to talk as a baby, failed the general part of the entry test, struggled at work initially ~ failures as a young man
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc đề cập đến việc “Einstein chậm nói khi còn nhỏ, trượt phần thi đầu vào phổ thông của trường Bách khoa Zurich, và gặp khó khăn lúc mới đi làm". Tuy nhiên, bài đọc không hề nhắc đến thông tin “do ông ta thiếu tự tin” trong câu hỏi. (Einstein's failures as a young man were due to his lack of confidence.)
Bước 4: Đáp án: NOT GIVEN
quotes: Einstein was slow to talk as a baby. He foiled the general part of the entry test to Zurich Polytechnic - though they let him in because of high physics and math scores. He struggled at work initially, but he kept plugging away and eventually rewrote the laws of Newtonian mechanics with his theory of relativity.

questions.text: It is difficult to reach agreement on whether some children are actually born gifted.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
(Người ta) khó mà có được sự đồng thuận về việc liệu một số trẻ em có thực sự là thiên tài bẩm sinh hay không.
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
jury is out ~ difficult to reach agreement
giftedness being innate ~ children are actually born gifted
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ "Trong khi vẫn còn nhiều tranh cãi liệu rằng tài năng có phải là do bẩm sinh hay không, và còn yếu tố nào khác tạo nên sự khác biệt hay không. Tuy nhiên, có một điều chắc chắn là: những hành vi mà dẫn đến thành tích xuất sắc đều có thể học tập và rèn luyện được". Điều này đồng nghĩa với thông tin trong câu hỏi "(người ta) khó mà có được sự đồng thuận về việc liệu rằng một số trẻ em có thực sự là thiên tài bẩm sinh không" trong câu hỏi. (It is difficult to reach agreement on whether some children are actually born gifted.)
Bước 4: Đáp án: YES
quotes: While the jury is out on giftedness being innate and other factors potentially making the difference, what is certain is that the behaviours associated with high levels of performance are replicable and most can be taught - even traits such as curiosity.

questions.text: Einstein was upset by the public's view of his life's work.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi
Einstein cảm thấy buồn về cách công chúng nhìn nhận thành tựu cả đời của ông.
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
Einstein ~ tên riêng giữ nguyên
most people say ~ public's view of his life's work
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc đề cập đến việc Einstein nhìn nhận nhiều người đã có quan điểm sai khi cho rằng trí tuệ là điều làm nên một nhà khoa học, và theo ông tính cách mới làm nên điều đó, nhưng không hề nhắc đến thông tin "Einstein cảm thấy buồn" trong câu hỏi. (Einstein was upset by the public's view of his life's work.)
Bước 4: Đáp án: NOT GIVEN
quotes: He once wrote: 'It's not that I'm so smart, it's just that I stay with problems longer. Most people say it is the intellect which makes a great scientist. They are wrong: it is character.

questions.text: Einstein put his success down to the speed at which he dealt with scientific questions.
questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu câu hỏi:
Einstein cho rằng thành công của ông là do tốc độ giải quyết các vấn đề khoa học.
Bước 2: Tìm các keywords được paraphrase trong bài:
Einstein ~ tên riêng giữ nguyên
He once wrote ~ put his success down to
stay with problems longer ~ speed at which he dealt with scientific questions
Bước 3: So sánh và đối chiếu:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ Einstein nói "Không phải tôi thông minh đến thế, mà là tôi kiên trì với vấn đề lâu hơn". Điều này trái ngược với thông tin trong câu hỏi "Einstein cho rằng thành công của ông là do tốc độ giải quyết các vấn đề khoa học" trong câu hỏi. (Einstein put his success down to the speed at which he dealt with scientific questions.)
Bước 4: Đáp án: NO
quotes: He once wrote: 'It's not that I'm so smart, it's just that I stay with problems longer. Most people say it is the intellect which makes a great scientist. They are wrong: it is character.

questions.text: What does Eyre believe is needed for children to equal 'gifted' standards?

options.label: A
options.text: strict discipline from the teaching staff

options.label: B
options.text: assistance from their peers in the classroom

options.label: C
options.text: the development of a spirit of inquiry towards their studies

options.label: D
options.text: the determination to surpass everyone else's achievements

questions.explanation:
Bước 1: Hiểu và tìm keywords trong câu hỏi:
Theo Eyre, trẻ em cần đáp ứng những điều kiện gì để đạt đến tiêu chuẩn của một ‘thiên tài’ (‘gifted’ standards’)?
Bước 2: Tìm thông tin dựa trên keywords:
Bài đọc chỉ rõ: “Các nghiên cứu mới nhất về thần kinh học và tâm lý học cho thấy hầu hết mọi người đều có thể đạt được mức độ thành tích tương đương với những học sinh được coi là thiên tài xuất sắc trong trường học. Tuy nhiên, họ cần được dạy thái độ và phương pháp học tập đúng đắn, đồng thời phát triển các phẩm chất của học sinh xuất sắc – chẳng hạn như tính tò mò, kiên trì và chăm chỉ”
=> Thông tin được in đậm đồng nghĩa với câu C (Sự nuôi dưỡng tinh thần ham học hỏi).
Bước 3: Đáp án: C
Bước 4: Giải thích đáp án gây nhiễu:
Đáp án A -> Đoạn văn không nhắc đến yếu tố “kỷ luật nghiêm khắc từ giáo viên”.
Đáp án B -> Đoạn văn không nhắc đến yếu tố “hỗ trợ từ bạn bè cùng lớp”.
Đáp án D -> Đoạn văn không nhắc đến yếu tố “quyết tâm đạt thành tích hơn các học sinh khác”.
quotes: However, they must be taught the right attitudes and approaches to their learning and develop the attributes of high performers - curiosity, persistence and hard work, for example - an approach Eyre calls 'high performance learning'.

questions.text: What is the result of Ericsson's research?

options.label: A
options.text: Very gifted students do not need to work on improving memory skills.

options.label: B
options.text: Being born with a special gift is not the key factor in becoming expert.

options.label: C
options.text: Including time for physical exercise is crucial in raising performance.

options.label: D
options.text: 10,000 hours of relevant and demanding work will create a genius.

quotes: After research going back to 1980 into diverse achievements, from music to memory to sport, he doesn't think unique and innate talents are at the heart of performance.

questions.text: In the penultimate paragraph, it is stated the key to some deprived children's success is

options.label: A
options.text: a regular and nourishing diet at home.

options.label: B
options.text: the loving support of more than one parent.

options.label: C
options.text: a community which has well-funded facilities for learning.

options.label: D
options.text: the guidance of someone who recognises the benefits of learning.

quotes: Interviews uncovered strong evidence of an adult or adults in the child's life who valued and supported education, either in the immediate or extended family or in the child's wider community.
